title: Battle of Cannae
summary: Hold the crescent, win both cavalry wings, close the double envelopment, then seize all three Roman camps before their reserves can restore the line.
teaching_goal: Nothing new is taught here. The ridge, the bait and the beheading are all things you already know; Cannae only asks whether you can run three of them at once against four times your number.
narrative_intent: Hannibal's masterpiece becomes a prolonged operational battle, not a single frontal collision: a Gallic and Iberian crescent that gives ground, African wings that hold, and Hasdrubal's heavy horse on the river flank.
historical_context: August 216 BC: beside the Aufidus the consuls crossed the river and drew up some eighty thousand men, the legions in the centre deeper than they were wide. Varro, in command that day, led the allied horse on the Roman left; Paullus led the Roman horse on the right by the river. Hannibal bowed his Gauls and Iberians out toward them in a crescent, set his Africans on the wings and screened the front with Balearic slingers. Hasdrubal's Iberian and Gallic horse broke Paullus by the river, rode behind the Roman army and fell on its rear as the crescent gave and the Africans turned inward. Paullus died on the field; Varro escaped to Venusia. Altered here: the Romans had two camps, not three, and the field towns and the Sepulcher graves are the game's.

victory_conditions.description: Crush all three Roman camps and seal the iron tomb shut. No escape.
Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.

defeat_conditions.description: Your command falls — and the wings fold inward.
Every soldier lost is counted by the enemy tonight.
The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.
A general alone on a dead field is just the last corpse standing.

optional_objectives.description: Break the old grave west of your hill before the Romans count its dead as theirs.

stages.title: Take the allied camp
stages.description: Turn the Roman allied camp south of the field, where Varro leads the allied horse.
stages.hint: It is the closest camp to your hill; take it before the wings close.

stages.title: Take the consular town
stages.description: Seize the consular town at the centre of the Roman line, behind the legions.
stages.hint: The centre gives way once the wings are wrapped around it. Put the Gauls and Iberians in Convex Crescent from the Formation panel: the centre bows out toward the enemy and gives ground under pressure while the Africans on the wings hold, as Hannibal's did.

stages.title: Take the river camp
stages.description: Close the encirclement on Paullus' camp across the Aufidus to the north.
stages.hint: The ford below the old wreck is shallow in August. With the river camp taken there is nowhere left for the legions to reform.

stages.title: Kill the consular commanders
stages.description: Finish the officers inside the ring: Paullus by the river, Varro with the allied horse, and the commander of the centre.
stages.hint: Their troops leave the field with them.

actions.text: Let the Gallic and Iberian crescent take the Roman centre and give ground slowly. Keep both cavalry wings active.
Paullus' reserves are crossing the Aufidus from the northern camp. Close the pocket faster.
Fresh Roman horse is coming up from the consular town and the allied camp. Keep your own cavalry between it and your centre.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Eighty thousand, and the command is mine today. Paullus looked at this plain and saw cavalry ground; I looked at the legions and saw the end of the war. He may keep the right by the river. I take the allied horse on the left myself.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: So the centre gave and the wings closed, and I rode out of it with seventy horse to Venusia. The Senate will come out to thank me for not despairing of the Republic. It is the strangest thanks a man was ever given, and I will take it.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: You bent us and we did not break, and that is the only sentence anyone will need. Gather your dead off the Aufidus. The river runs slow here; they will be a long time going by.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: You have the allied camp. Socii - allies. I promised them land for this war, and you have just handed them the first piece of it face down.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: The consular town. Varro is not in it; Varro is out on the left with the allied horse, being brave at other people. Enjoy the walls. We never needed them.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The Aufidus camp. So the ring closes. Tell the Senate to fortify the city. Tell Fabius I kept his counsel to the end. I stay here with my men.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: Here they come - the whole consular line, deeper than it is wide, at Varro's tempo. Eighty thousand men do not turn. Remember that when you want them to.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: My allies are at your works. Italians, mostly. They fight for Rome because the alternative is fighting Rome, which is a very persuasive argument. I make it often.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Your centre is going down. Of course it is: you put the Gauls there, and Gauls are for spending. My legions will walk through the hole by noon.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Hannibal is down. Fabius said wait. Paullus said wait. The butcher's son from the Forum said fight, and here we are.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The allied horse is down to a handful and Hasdrubal's riders are behind it. There is a road to Venusia. A consul who lives can raise another army; a dead one only gets a statue.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: Let the centre give. The Gauls and Iberians bow out toward them, the Africans wait on the wings, Hasdrubal has the river. Eighty thousand men walk into a sack as easily as into a field.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: The allied wing has lost its consul. Varro will not see Venusia. Turn that wing inward.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: Their centre has nowhere left to step back. Open the ring for no one.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The Roman horse is with me by the river. Varro wanted this battle; I will fight it properly all the same. Close up on the bank. Do not let Hasdrubal through.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: Paullus is dead. He would not take a horse to leave the field. Find his body and bury it with honour; Rome kept the wrong consul.

theme: The battlefield becomes a closing iron tomb.
